title: Weekends Ruining Your Progress? How to Stay on Track Without Feeling Restricted
intro: Yes, weekends can wipe out a whole week of progress. But the cause isn't that you eat nice food, it's the 'might as well' mood from Friday night to Sunday, and that can be managed without you having to lock yourself at home.

sections.h: Why the scale goes up every Monday
sections.p: From Monday to Friday, you might cut an estimated 300-500 kcal a day. If Saturday and Sunday are each about 1,000 kcal over, almost all that effort is gone. Salty food and late-night eating also make your body hold water. So the Monday increase is usually a mix of water and extra calories, not all of it fat.

sections.h: Choose just one or two 'treat meals'
sections.p: You don't have to say no to brunch with friends or a big family meal. Just decide early when you want to eat more, for example a kenduri dinner on Saturday. For your other meals that day, eat as usual. For example, a breakfast with protein and a nasi campur lunch with a normal portion.

At a buffet or kenduri, take protein dishes and vegetables first, then the rice. Share desserts and kuih with others. One glass of sweet drink is enough, then switch to plain water or teh o kosong. Eat slowly and stop when you feel 80% full.

sections.h: On weekends, your steps usually drop
sections.p: On workdays you walk to the parking, to the pantry and to meetings. On weekends, many people just lepak on the sofa. Try walking around the mall, bringing the kids to the park or walking to the pasar pagi. Small movements like these count too.

sections.h: If you've already overeaten, what now?
sections.p: Don't 'punish' yourself by skipping meals or starving the next day. That usually makes you eat more at night. Just carry on with your usual routine at your next meal. One weekend won't ruin all your effort, what matters is your overall pattern.

action: Set one free meal for this weekend, and plan your other meals as usual.
Eat a breakfast with protein before leaving the house, for example 2 eggs with bread.
Aim for an estimated 7,000 steps on Saturday and Sunday.
Limit sweet drinks to one glass a day on weekends.
Weigh yourself on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, then look at the average, not just one number.
myth: Many believe a 'cheat day' can 'reset' your metabolism. Actually, one day of eating a lot doesn't reset anything, it just adds calories, so being flexible is okay but not compulsory.

faq.q: My weight went up 1-2 kg after the weekend. Is that fat?
faq.a: Usually it's mostly water and food still in your stomach, especially after eating salty food and carbs. It usually comes back down within 2-3 days if you return to your usual routine.

faq.q: Do I need to watch what I eat 7 days a week without a break?
faq.a: No need to be strict all the time. What matters is that your weekly average is still in a small deficit. Having room for treat meals makes it easier to stay consistent in the long run.

faq.q: What if I have a kenduri every week?
faq.a: Treat the kenduri as that week's 'treat meal'. Take half a plate of rice, more protein dishes and vegetables. Keep your other meals that day simple and balanced.
